intended_use_case: An AI agent that reads channel history and posts replies in customers' Slack workspaces
overview: Slack apps are installed per workspace through an OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow that grants a bot token (and optionally user tokens) with the scopes you request. Registering the app and enabling distribution to other workspaces is self-serve, with no review documented for unlisted distribution. The catch for AI agents: since May 2025, commercially distributed apps that are not in the Slack Marketplace get 1 request per minute (15 objects) on conversations.history and conversations.replies for new installs. If your agent reads message history at any volume, plan for Marketplace listing, which requires 10+ active workspaces before you can submit and has a documented review of up to 10 business days plus up to 10 weeks.

recommended_path.summary: For a multi-tenant agent, register your own Slack app (custom OAuth app) so the consent screen shows your brand and you control scopes. Use a managed OAuth app from an integration platform only to prototype, and check that platform's Slack scopes and rate-limit treatment first.

options.title: Register your own Slack app
options.summary: Create the app, request bot/user scopes, implement the OAuth v2 install flow, and activate distribution.
options.when_to_choose: Production multi-tenant agents, custom scopes, your own branding, and eventual Marketplace listing.
tradeoffs: You own Marketplace review if you need higher history rate limits
Scope changes on a listed app require re-review

options.title: Use an integration platform's managed Slack app
options.summary: A platform supplies the registered app and stores tokens; your users still authorize their workspace.
options.when_to_choose: Prototypes and early pilots where speed matters more than branding or scope control.
tradeoffs: Consent screen shows the platform's app, not yours
Rate-limit treatment depends on whether the platform's app is Marketplace-approved (not verified here)

effort_estimate.basis: Recomputed from steps at load time.

external_wait.summary: None for unlisted distribution; up to 10 business days + up to 10 weeks if you list in the Slack Marketplace.
external_wait.explanation: Slack documents no review for unlisted distribution. Marketplace review has a preliminary stage (up to 10 business days) and a functional stage (up to 10 weeks for new apps); the queue position resets on resubmission during the preliminary stage, and Slack cannot expedite it.

approval_summary: No Slack approval is needed to register the app or distribute it unlisted. Marketplace review is required only if you want a Marketplace listing, which matters for agents because unlisted commercial apps get much lower history rate limits. Individual workspaces may also require admin approval to install.

prerequisites.title: A Slack workspace for development
prerequisites.detail: New apps can only be installed in their associated workspace until you enable distribution.

prerequisites.title: HTTPS endpoints
prerequisites.detail: Your OAuth redirect URL and the app's request URLs must use HTTPS/SSL before other workspaces can install the app.

prerequisites.title: Privacy policy and support page (for Marketplace)
prerequisites.detail: Marketplace apps need a public privacy policy describing third-party data handling and an accessible support channel.

setup_steps.title: Create the Slack app in your development workspace
setup_steps.explanation: Create a new app from Slack's app management pages and associate it with a workspace you control. Note the client ID and client secret on the app's credentials page.
setup_steps.why_it_matters: Every install, scope, and redirect URL hangs off this app record.
setup_steps.expected_outcome: An app with a client ID and secret, installable only in your workspace.

setup_steps.title: Choose minimal bot and user scopes
setup_steps.explanation: Decide which actions run as the bot (scope=) and which need to act as a user (user_scope=). Request the smallest set that supports your agent; scopes are additive per install and cannot be removed from a token without revoking it.
setup_steps.why_it_matters: Workspace admins and Marketplace reviewers judge the app by its scopes; over-asking blocks installs and reviews.
setup_steps.expected_outcome: A justified list of bot and user scopes.

setup_steps.title: Configure an HTTPS redirect URL
setup_steps.explanation: Add your OAuth callback under OAuth & Permissions. Slack requires redirect URLs to use HTTPS.
setup_steps.why_it_matters: A missing or non-HTTPS redirect breaks every install.
setup_steps.expected_outcome: Redirect URL saved and matching what your code sends.

setup_steps.title: Implement the OAuth v2 install flow and token storage
setup_steps.explanation: Send users to slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize with your client ID and scopes, receive the temporary code (valid ten minutes), exchange it at oauth.v2.access, and store the bot/user tokens securely per workspace. Tokens do not expire unless you opt into token rotation.
setup_steps.why_it_matters: This is the integration your users touch; mistakes here surface as failed installs.
setup_steps.expected_outcome: Installing from your site stores a working token for the workspace.

setup_steps.title: Check whether your agent depends on message history
setup_steps.explanation: If the agent calls conversations.history or conversations.replies, new installs of a commercially distributed non-Marketplace app are limited to 1 request per minute and 15 objects per request. Decide now whether you will pursue Marketplace listing.
setup_steps.why_it_matters: This limit can make a history-reading agent unusable without Marketplace approval.
setup_steps.expected_outcome: A decision: unlisted distribution is enough, or Marketplace listing is required.

setup_steps.title: Activate public (unlisted) distribution
setup_steps.explanation: In Manage Distribution, complete the checklist (HTTPS for all URLs, OAuth flow in place) and activate public distribution to get an installable Add to Slack link.
setup_steps.why_it_matters: Without distribution the app can only be installed in its own workspace.
setup_steps.expected_outcome: A shareable install link that works for other workspaces.

setup_steps.title: Install on a second workspace as a new customer would
setup_steps.explanation: Install, onboard, use, and uninstall the app on a workspace that is not your development workspace. Include a workspace where only admins can approve installs.
setup_steps.why_it_matters: Admin-restricted workspaces and fresh installs reveal problems your dev workspace hides.
setup_steps.expected_outcome: Clean install/uninstall on an external workspace, including the admin-approval path.

setup_steps.title: Prepare a Marketplace submission (if listing)
setup_steps.explanation: Reach 10+ active workspaces, publish a privacy policy and support page, record a demo video of install, OAuth, set-up and uninstall, and prepare reviewer test accounts (including paid access if your service needs it).
setup_steps.why_it_matters: Submissions that are not production-ready are returned, and the preliminary queue position resets on resubmission.
setup_steps.expected_outcome: A submission that meets Slack's published requirements.

setup_steps.title: Submit for Marketplace review and respond to feedback
setup_steps.explanation: Submit from the app settings. Expect preliminary feedback within about 10 business days and functional review within about 10 weeks for a new app; the review cannot be expedited.
setup_steps.why_it_matters: This is the long pole in the timeline; submit well before launch.
setup_steps.expected_outcome: Approval, after which you choose when to publish.

setup_steps.title: Plan for locked configuration after listing
setup_steps.explanation: Once published, the live app's configuration, features and scopes are locked; changes need re-review. Keep a staging app for testing updates.
setup_steps.why_it_matters: Adding a scope later can break installs if it is not reviewed first.
setup_steps.expected_outcome: A release process that includes Slack re-review for scope changes.

approval_and_distribution.applies_when: You want a Marketplace listing (needed for normal history rate limits on new installs)
approval_and_distribution.description: Requires 10+ active workspaces before submitting, then preliminary and functional review.

testing_plan.title: Install from a clean external workspace
testing_plan.detail: Run install, onboarding, usage and uninstall as a brand-new customer would.

testing_plan.title: Exercise the admin-approval path
testing_plan.detail: Test in a workspace where only admins can approve apps, so you see the request flow.

testing_plan.title: Measure history calls under the non-Marketplace limit
testing_plan.detail: Simulate your agent's reads at 1 request per minute and 15 objects to see whether it stays useful.

blockers_and_unknowns.title: History rate limits for unlisted commercial apps
blockers_and_unknowns.detail: New installs of commercially distributed non-Marketplace apps get 1 request per minute and at most 15 objects for conversations.history and conversations.replies.
blockers_and_unknowns.mitigation: Pursue Marketplace listing, or design the agent around events instead of history reads.

blockers_and_unknowns.title: 10 active workspaces before Marketplace submission
blockers_and_unknowns.detail: You cannot submit until the app is active in 10+ workspaces, so you need an unlisted pilot first.
blockers_and_unknowns.mitigation: Run a pilot with early customers via unlisted distribution.

blockers_and_unknowns.title: Long, non-expeditable review
blockers_and_unknowns.detail: Functional review can take up to 10 weeks for new apps and cannot be accelerated.
blockers_and_unknowns.mitigation: Submit as early as possible and keep the submission production-ready.

blockers_and_unknowns.title: Whether your specific scopes will be approved
blockers_and_unknowns.detail: Slack reviews scope justifications case by case; the checked pages do not predict outcomes.
blockers_and_unknowns.mitigation: Request least-privilege scopes and justify each one in the submission.

context_variations.personal: Install the app only in your own workspace; no distribution or review is needed, and the non-Marketplace history limit targets commercially distributed apps rather than internal ones.
context_variations.internal: Keep the app undistributed in your company's workspace. Slack says internal customer-built apps should not see the 2025 history rate-limit changes. Admin approval may still apply.
context_variations.multi_tenant_saas: Enable distribution for a pilot, then plan Marketplace listing if the agent reads history, since new unlisted installs face 1 request/minute limits.

claims.statement: Apps request scopes by redirecting users to https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize; bot scopes go in the scope parameter and user scopes in user_scope.
claims.evidence_quote: To request scopes, redirect Slack users to https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize

claims.statement: The OAuth redirect_uri must use HTTPS.
claims.evidence_quote: The redirect_uri must use HTTPS.

claims.statement: The temporary authorization code expires after ten minutes and is exchanged using oauth.v2.access.
claims.evidence_quote: That's your temporary authorization code, which expires after ten minutes.

claims.statement: Slack OAuth tokens do not expire by default; they are revoked on uninstall or when no longer needed.
claims.evidence_quote: OAuth tokens do not expire. If they are no longer needed, they can be revoked.

claims.statement: Apps using granular permissions can opt into token rotation (refresh token plus expiring access token).
claims.evidence_quote: for Slack apps using granular permissions, you can exchange your access token for a refresh token and an expiring access token with

claims.statement: Scopes cannot be removed from an existing token without revoking it.
claims.evidence_quote: There is no way to remove scopes from an existing token without revoking it entirely.

claims.statement: User tokens let an app act directly on behalf of users when necessary.
claims.evidence_quote: User tokens allow you to work directly on behalf of users when necessary.

claims.statement: A newly built Slack app can only be installed in its associated workspace until distribution is set up.
claims.evidence_quote: By default, a newly built Slack app can only be installed in its associated workspace

claims.statement: Unlisted distribution suits pilots with early customers; apps intended for commercial distribution should be submitted and approved for Marketplace listing.
claims.evidence_quote: Distributing your unlisted app is perfect for when you want to test out your app by running a pilot for early customers; however, apps intended for commercial distribution should be submitted and approved for listing in the Slack Marketplace.

claims.statement: Unlike unlisted distributed apps, Marketplace-listed apps are reviewed against Slack's requirements and guidelines.
claims.evidence_quote: Unlike unlisted distributed apps, apps listed in the Slack Marketplace are reviewed against our

claims.statement: Apps open to installation by other workspaces must support SSL for their URLs.
claims.evidence_quote: Slack apps open to installation by other workspaces have additional security requirements. Your app must support SSL for all of the following URLs:

claims.statement: Some workspaces restrict installation to workspace administrators, and some allow only Marketplace-listed apps.
claims.evidence_quote: Some workspaces will restrict app installation so that only workspace administrators can provide authorization.

claims.statement: Before Marketplace submission, the app must be installed on 10 or more active workspaces (used in the past 28 days); apps below this are blocked from submitting.
claims.evidence_quote: Your app has been installed on 10 or more active workspaces
claims.note: S4 states the same threshold: apps installed on less than 10 active workspaces with less than 10 weekly active users are not accepted.

claims.statement: Marketplace preliminary review takes up to 10 business days; functional review takes up to 10 weeks for new submissions and 6 weeks for resubmitted changes.
claims.evidence_quote: Currently, the preliminary part of the review takes up to 10 business days to receive feedback, while the functional review takes up to 10 weeks for new submissions and 6 weeks for published apps resubmitting changes.

claims.statement: During the preliminary review, your queue position resets each time you resubmit.
claims.evidence_quote: During this part of the review, your place in the queue is reset each time you resubmit.

claims.statement: Slack cannot skip or accelerate Marketplace review to match a launch date.
claims.evidence_quote: We are unable to skip or accelerate the review process in order to coordinate with your launch

claims.statement: After publication, the live Marketplace app's configuration, features and scopes are locked; changes require re-submission.
claims.evidence_quote: Once your app is published in the Slack Marketplace, the live version of your app is locked.

claims.statement: Marketplace apps must have a clear privacy policy describing how third-party data is handled.
claims.evidence_quote: All Slack Marketplace apps must include a clear privacy policy that details how third-party data is handled

claims.statement: For commercially distributed non-Marketplace apps, conversations.history and conversations.replies are limited to 1 request per minute with at most 15 objects per request for new apps and new installs (from 2025-05-29).
claims.evidence_quote: The new rate limits will be updated to allow 1 request per minute and will return a maximum of 15 objects per request.
claims.note: S6 (Rate limits) also states that non-Marketplace apps are subject to the changed limits while Marketplace and internal customer-built apps are not.

claims.statement: The reduced limits apply only to apps commercially distributed outside the Marketplace (unlisted apps); Marketplace-approved and internal customer-built apps are not affected.
claims.evidence_quote: This rate limit reduction will apply only to applications that are commercially distributed outside of the Marketplace

claims.statement: Slack asks Marketplace apps to request the smallest number of least-permissive scopes.
claims.evidence_quote: Focus on requesting the smallest number of least permissive scopes you can while still providing a good experience.

claims.statement: Reviewers need test credentials; if your service requires a paid account you must share credentials with the required access.
claims.evidence_quote: If a paid account is required for your service, you’ll need to share login credentials with us for an account with the required level of access.

claims.statement: For new submissions, Slack asks for a video showing installation, OAuth, set-up, end-to-end use and uninstallation.
claims.evidence_quote: For a new submission, it should include a video showing the full installation and OAuth flow, set-up process, and end-to-end functionality, including uninstallation.
